en.27:15: Now it was the governor’s custom at the feast to release to the crowd a prisoner of their choosing.
en.27:16: At that time they were holding a notorious prisoner named Barabbas.
en.27:17: So when the crowd had assembled, Pilate asked them, “Which one do you want me to release to you: Barabbas, or Jesus who is called Christ?”
en.27:18: For he knew it was out of envy that they had handed Jesus over to him.
en.27:19: While Pilate was sitting on the judgment seat, his wife sent him this message: “Have nothing to do with that innocent man, for I have suffered terribly in a dream today because of Him.”
en.27:20: But the chief priests and elders persuaded the crowds to ask for Barabbas and to have Jesus put to death.
en.27:21: “Which of the two do you want me to release to you?” asked the governor. “Barabbas,” they replied.
en.27:22: “What then should I do with Jesus who is called Christ?” Pilate asked. They all answered, “Crucify Him!”
en.27:23: “Why?” asked Pilate. “What evil has He done?” But they shouted all the louder, “Crucify Him!”
en.27:24: When Pilate saw that he was accomplishing nothing, but that instead a riot was breaking out, he took water and washed his hands before the crowd. “I am innocent of this man’s blood,” he said. “You bear the responsibility.”
en.27:25: All the people answered, “His blood be on us and on our children!”
en.27:26: So Pilate released Barabbas to them. But he had Jesus flogged, and handed Him over to be crucified.

en.15:6: Now it was Pilate’s custom at the feast to release to the people a prisoner of their choosing.
en.15:7: And a man named Barabbas was imprisoned with the rebels who had committed murder during the insurrection.
en.15:8: So the crowd went up and began asking Pilate to keep his custom.
en.15:9: “Do you want me to release to you the King of the Jews?” Pilate asked.
en.15:10: For he knew it was out of envy that the chief priests had handed Jesus over.
en.15:11: But the chief priests stirred up the crowd to have him release Barabbas to them instead.
en.15:12: So Pilate asked them again, “What then do you want me to do with the One you call the King of the Jews?”
en.15:14: “Why?” asked Pilate. “What evil has He done?” But they shouted all the louder, “Crucify Him!”
en.15:15: And wishing to satisfy the crowd, Pilate released Barabbas to them. But he had Jesus flogged, and handed Him over to be crucified.

en.23:18: But they all cried out in unison: “Away with this man! Release Barabbas to us!”
en.23:19: (Barabbas had been imprisoned for an insurrection in the city, and for murder.)
en.23:20: Wanting to release Jesus, Pilate addressed them again,
en.23:21: but they kept shouting, “Crucify Him! Crucify Him!”
en.23:22: A third time he said to them, “What evil has this man done? I have found in Him no offense worthy of death. So after I punish Him, I will release Him.”
en.23:23: But they were insistent, demanding with loud voices for Jesus to be crucified. And their clamor prevailed.
en.23:24: So Pilate sentenced that their demand be met.
en.23:25: As they had requested, he released the one imprisoned for insurrection and murder, and he handed Jesus over to their will.

en.18:39: But it is your custom that I release to you one prisoner at the Passover. So then, do you want me to release to you the King of the Jews?”
en.18:40: “Not this man,” they shouted, “but Barabbas!” (Now Barabbas was an insurrectionist.)
en.19:1: Then Pilate took Jesus and had Him flogged.
en.19:2: The soldiers twisted together a crown of thorns, set it on His head, and dressed Him in a purple robe.
en.19:3: And they went up to Him again and again, saying, “Hail, King of the Jews!” and slapping Him in the face.
en.19:4: Once again Pilate came out and said to the Jews, “Look, I am bringing Him out to you to let you know that I find no basis for a charge against Him.”
en.19:5: When Jesus came out wearing the crown of thorns and the purple robe, Pilate said to them, “Here is the man!”
en.19:6: As soon as the chief priests and officers saw Him, they shouted, “Crucify Him! Crucify Him!” “You take Him and crucify Him,” Pilate replied, “for I find no basis for a charge against Him.”
en.19:7: “We have a law,” answered the Jews, “and according to that law He must die, because He declared Himself to be the Son of God.”
en.19:8: When Pilate heard this statement, he was even more afraid,
en.19:9: and he went back into the Praetorium. “Where are You from?” he asked. But Jesus gave no answer.
en.19:10: So Pilate said to Him, “Do You refuse to speak to me? Do You not know that I have authority to release You and authority to crucify You?”
en.19:11: Jesus answered, “You would have no authority over Me if it were not given to you from above. Therefore the one who handed Me over to you is guilty of greater sin.”
en.19:12: From then on, Pilate tried to release Him, but the Jews kept shouting, “If you release this man, you are no friend of Caesar. Anyone who declares himself a king is defying Caesar.”
en.19:13: When Pilate heard these words, he brought Jesus out and sat on the judgment seat at a place called the Stone Pavement, which in Hebrew is Gabbatha.
en.19:14: It was the day of Preparation for the Passover, about the sixth hour. And Pilate said to the Jews, “Here is your King!”
en.19:15: At this, they shouted, “Away with Him! Away with Him! Crucify Him!” “Shall I crucify your King?” Pilate asked. “We have no king but Caesar,” replied the chief priests.
en.19:16: Then Pilate handed Jesus over to be crucified, and the soldiers took Him away.
